courses.title: Common Core Training
courses.short_description: The mandatory foundation for every VTIARA role: values, hygiene, consent, privacy and emergency awareness.
courses.overview: Common Core is the shared foundation every VTIARA team member completes before role training. It covers how we present ourselves, how we speak with patients, and the hygiene, infection-control, consent and privacy habits that keep every patient safe. It ends with a 20-question knowledge test and a supervised hand-hygiene practical.
courses.audience: Every new and existing VTIARA team member, and future trainees from outside the clinic, regardless of final role.
eligibility: Willingness to attend the academy practical session
outcomes: Explain VTIARA values and uphold grooming and presentation standards
Communicate with patients clearly, kindly and within role scope
Describe skin and hair basics without diagnosing or advising treatment
Perform hand hygiene correctly and apply infection-control precautions
Segregate biomedical waste correctly
Obtain and respect consent, privacy and confidentiality
Respond to fire and medical emergencies by escalating promptly
requirements_text: 80% or higher on the 20-question knowledge test

lessons.title: VTIARA values and standards
lessons.description: What 'One Standard' means across every role and branch.
lessons.transcript: Welcome to VTIARA. Our standard is the same in every room and every role: safe, respectful, consistent care. In this lesson we walk through the VTIARA values and how they show up in everyday decisions.

lessons.title: Grooming and professional presentation
lessons.description: Uniform, grooming, jewellery, nails and personal hygiene expectations.
lessons.transcript: Your presentation tells patients how seriously we take their care. We cover uniform, nails, hair, jewellery and personal hygiene, and why each matters in a clinical setting.

modules.title: Patient communication and skin & hair basics

lessons.title: Patient communication
lessons.description: Greeting, listening, empathy, and knowing when to hand over to a clinician.
lessons.transcript: Good communication starts with a warm greeting and active listening. If a patient asks a clinical question, you acknowledge it and refer them to the doctor. You never diagnose or prescribe.

lessons.title: Skin and hair basics
lessons.description: Plain-language structure of skin and hair, to support — never replace — clinical advice.
lessons.transcript: This lesson gives you a shared vocabulary for skin layers, the hair growth cycle and common concerns, so you can understand your colleagues and support patients within your role.

lessons.title: Hand hygiene: the five moments
lessons.description: When and how to clean hands; rub versus wash; common mistakes.
lessons.transcript: Clean hands before touching a patient, before a clean or aseptic task, after body-fluid exposure, after touching a patient and after touching patient surroundings. Rub for 20 to 30 seconds, or wash for 40 to 60 seconds when hands are visibly soiled.

lessons.title: Infection control and biomedical waste
lessons.description: Standard precautions, PPE, safe sharps handling and colour-coded waste segregation.
lessons.transcript: Treat every patient with standard precautions. Sharps go in a puncture-proof container without recapping. Segregate waste at the point of generation using the colour-coded system.

lessons.title: Consent, privacy and confidentiality
lessons.description: Informed consent, patient photos, data safety and what never to share.
lessons.transcript: Consent must be informed, voluntary and documented. Patient information is shared only with those who need it, in private, and photos are taken only with consent on approved devices.

lessons.title: Fire and emergency awareness
lessons.description: Raising the alarm, evacuation, and escalating medical emergencies.
lessons.transcript: If a patient collapses or a fire starts, raise the alarm, stay calm and follow the clinic emergency plan. Your role is to escalate quickly and support, not to treat.

questions.q: How long should you rub alcohol-based hand rub over all hand surfaces?
o: Only until it stops feeling wet
questions.e: Alcohol-based rub needs 20–30 seconds of contact and should be rubbed until your hands are dry.

questions.q: Your hands are visibly soiled. What should you use?
questions.e: Visibly soiled hands must be washed with soap and water; rub is not enough.

questions.q: Which is one of the five moments for hand hygiene?
o: Only at the start of your shift
questions.e: The five moments include before touching a patient, before a clean/aseptic task, after body-fluid exposure, after touching a patient and after touching patient surroundings.

questions.q: After removing gloves you should:
o: Do nothing, gloves kept hands clean
questions.e: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene. Clean your hands after removing them.

questions.q: Standard precautions apply to:
o: Only patients who ask for them
questions.e: Standard precautions treat every patient's blood and body fluids as potentially infectious.

questions.q: A reusable instrument has just been used on a patient. What do you do?
o: Wipe it and use it on the next patient
Treat it as contaminated and send it for decontamination per protocol
Rinse under the tap and keep it on the tray
Leave it in the treatment room
questions.e: Used instruments are contaminated until they go through the clinic's decontamination and sterilisation process.

questions.q: Where do used needles and other sharps go?
questions.e: Sharps go into a puncture-proof, leak-proof sharps container (white translucent under the Bio-Medical Waste Rules).

questions.q: You have just used a needle. What must you never do?
o: Dispose of it immediately in the sharps container
Recap or bend it by hand
Keep the container below fill line
questions.e: Never recap or bend needles; this is a leading cause of needle-stick injuries.

questions.q: Blood-soiled cotton and dressings are segregated into:
questions.e: Soiled waste such as blood-stained cotton and dressings goes into the yellow category bag.

questions.q: Before any procedure, patient consent must be:
o: Assumed if the patient booked an appointment
Informed, voluntary and documented as per clinic policy
Taken verbally from a relative only
questions.e: Valid consent is informed, voluntary and recorded before the procedure begins.

questions.q: A patient hesitates and asks you to stop during a procedure. You:
o: Finish quickly as it is almost done
Stop and inform the doctor or supervisor
Ignore it if they are quiet
questions.e: Consent can be withdrawn at any time. Stop safely and escalate.

questions.q: You need a photo of a patient's treatment area for the record. You:
o: Use your personal phone for convenience
Take it only with the patient's consent on an approved clinic device
Ask a colleague to take it on theirs
Skip consent if the face is not visible
questions.e: Photos need explicit consent and must be taken and stored only on approved clinic systems.

questions.q: A friend asks whether a well-known person visited the clinic. You:
o: Say nothing is confirmed or shared about any patient
questions.e: Never confirm or hint at who is or is not a patient.

questions.q: Patient details may be discussed:
o: Only with those who need to know, in a private place
questions.e: Share on a need-to-know basis and in private settings only.

questions.q: A colleague asks to use your system login 'just this once'. You:
o: Refuse; every user must use their own login
Share it and change it later
Write it on a sticky note for them
questions.e: Logins are personal. Sharing breaks audit trails and patient privacy.

questions.q: You step away from a computer showing a patient record. You should:
o: Ask the patient to watch it
questions.e: Lock the screen every time you leave a device.

questions.q: A patient asks which tablet to take for hair fall. You:
o: Suggest one you have heard works
Politely explain you cannot advise and connect them with the doctor
questions.e: Only qualified clinicians diagnose or prescribe. Refer clinical questions to the doctor.

questions.q: An upset patient complains about waiting. Your best first step is to:
o: Argue the wait was not long
Listen calmly, acknowledge the concern and escalate if unresolved
questions.e: Listening and acknowledging calms the situation; escalate to your supervisor when needed.

questions.q: A patient feels faint and slumps in the waiting area. You first:
o: Stay with the patient and alert the clinical team immediately
Wait to see if it passes
questions.e: Stay with the patient, call for help and follow the emergency protocol. Do not give medication.

questions.q: You discover a fire. What is the correct action?
o: Raise the alarm, alert others and follow the evacuation plan
questions.e: Raise the alarm, help others to safety and follow the evacuation plan.

items.label: Applies adequate product and covers all hand surfaces
Palm-to-palm, backs of hands and between fingers
Correct duration (20–30 s rub or 40–60 s wash)
Dries hands properly / rub left to dry

courses.title: Skin Therapist Training
courses.short_description: An eight-week structured programme to become a Level 1 Certified Therapist with supervised floor practice.
courses.overview: This programme builds safe, consistent skin and hair therapy skills in the VTIARA way. You will learn the science, consultation and documentation, then practise facials, skin treatments, scalp care and device handling under direct supervision, finishing with practical stations and a completed logbook.
courses.audience: Aspiring and existing skin therapists, and cosmetology or aesthetics trainees joining VTIARA.
eligibility: Common Core Training completed (recommended before starting)
Comfort working with patients in a clinical setting
outcomes: Apply skin and hair science to safe therapy decisions within scope
Conduct structured consultations and complete accurate documentation
Perform facials, skin treatments and scalp care to VTIARA standard under supervision
Operate devices with laser-safety precautions
Explain products and aftercare without prescribing
Demonstrate consistent practice through a supervised logbook

questions.q: A client shows a changing mole during a facial. You should:
o: Pause and refer the client to the doctor
questions.e: Anything outside therapist scope, including suspicious lesions, is referred to the doctor.

questions.q: Before a laser treatment starts, everyone in the room must:
questions.e: Correct protective eyewear is mandatory for all persons in the laser room.

questions.q: When should a procedure be recorded?
o: At the end of the week
Promptly and accurately after the procedure
questions.e: Timely, accurate records protect the patient and the clinic.

questions.q: The outermost layer of the skin is the:
questions.e: The epidermis is the outermost layer and forms the skin barrier.

courses.title: Staff Nurse Training
courses.short_description: Sterilisation, procedure assistance, medication safety and emergency readiness for nurses in a dermatology setting.
courses.overview: Designed for registered nurses joining VTIARA. You will standardise sterilisation and instrument processing, documentation, consent and photography, medication safety, procedure assistance and emergency response including BLS, followed by supervised practice and a practical examination.
courses.audience: Registered nurses (GNM or B.Sc Nursing) joining or working at VTIARA clinics.
eligibility: Verified State Nursing Council registration (upload your registration document at sign-up)
Common Core Training completed (recommended before starting)
outcomes: Process and sterilise instruments to clinic standard
Document, take consent and manage clinical photographs correctly
Apply medication-safety checks
Assist procedures safely within scope and Medical Advisor direction
Respond to emergencies and deliver BLS
Provide aftercare instructions as directed by the doctor
requirements_text: BLS renewal required to keep certificate valid

questions.q: Recommended adult chest-compression rate in BLS is:
questions.e: Adult BLS uses 100–120 compressions per minute.

questions.q: Adult compression depth should be about:
questions.e: Compress about 5–6 cm with full recoil.

questions.q: Before administering any medication you must confirm:
o: Right patient, drug, dose, route and time
That a colleague used it yesterday
questions.e: The medication 'rights' are verified every time.

questions.q: A sterilised pack has a chemical indicator that did not change colour. You:
o: Treat the pack as non-sterile and reprocess it
questions.e: An indicator failure means sterility is not assured. Do not use and reprocess.

courses.title: Housekeeping Training
courses.short_description: Clinical-grade cleaning, chemical safety, spill response and laser-room precautions, with a supervised practical.
courses.overview: Cleaning in a clinic is part of patient safety. This six-day programme covers cleaning routines, chemical safety and disinfectants, spill management, biomedical waste, linen handling and laser-room precautions, with supervised practical work signed off by a trainer.
courses.audience: Housekeeping and facility staff at VTIARA clinics and the academy.
eligibility: Common Core Training completed (recommended before starting)
Able to follow written and verbal safety instructions
outcomes: Follow validated cleaning routines for clinical areas
Handle and dilute chemicals and disinfectants safely
Respond correctly to spills and biohazards
Segregate biomedical waste and handle linen safely
Observe laser-room precautions

lessons.description: Hand hygiene, PPE and waste segregation.

lessons.title: Clean-to-dirty cleaning and room turnover
lessons.description: Sequence, high-touch surfaces and checklists.

lessons.title: Dilution, labelling and chemical safety
lessons.description: Never mix chemicals; correct contact times.

lessons.title: Spill response
lessons.description: Blood and body-fluid spill steps.

lessons.title: Laser-room cleaning precautions
lessons.description: Signage, eyewear and reflective surfaces.

questions.q: Which must you never mix?
questions.e: Mixing bleach with ammonia or acids can release toxic gas.

questions.q: You find a blood spill. First you:
o: Wipe it with a dry cloth
Wear PPE, contain and treat the spill per protocol
Cover it with a towel and leave
Ask a patient to avoid it
questions.e: Wear PPE, contain and disinfect using the clinic's spill procedure.

questions.q: When cleaning a treatment room you work:
o: Clean to dirty, top to bottom
questions.e: Clean-to-dirty and top-to-bottom avoids spreading contamination.

questions.q: In a laser room with the 'laser in use' sign lit, you:
o: Do not enter until the treatment ends and it is declared safe
questions.e: Never enter while the laser is in use; follow the room's safety instructions.

courses.title: Telecaller Training
courses.short_description: Patient communication, ethical selling, privacy and DND compliance, with mock calls and monitored live calls.
courses.overview: Telecallers are often a patient's first contact with VTIARA. This programme covers patient communication, treatment-knowledge boundaries, call scripts, CRM use, ethical selling, privacy and DND compliance, followed by mock calls and a period of monitored live calls before approval.
eligibility: Common Core Training completed (recommended before starting)
Good spoken communication in English and at least one local language
outcomes: Communicate clearly, respectfully and within knowledge boundaries
Use approved scripts and the CRM correctly
Sell ethically without guarantees or clinical advice
Protect patient privacy and comply with DND regulations
Handle live calls to the clinic's quality standard

o: Send a promotional SMS from a personal number
questions.e: Promotional calls to numbers on the DND registry are not allowed without valid consent.

questions.q: A caller asks whether a treatment will 'definitely' cure their problem. You:

Avoid guarantees and invite them for a doctor consultation
questions.e: Never guarantee outcomes. Invite the patient for a consultation.

questions.e: Telecallers never diagnose or prescribe.
